## Motivation

I still remember that my first scientific code was `Fortran 77` bisection method written in the lab with quintessil CRT screen with desktop fan guzzling making it evident that colling is going on. Next, was having lab notebook to capture important conceptual (semantic knowledge) notes like why relative error not absolute error as convergence criteria, what will happen if max iteration limit is not set, typical notes that don't find its way in code comments. Fast forward there is paradig shift now, coding agennts now do a fantastic job in writign codes, but the capturing semantic informations still remains as fundamental to process as was was then, information that helps humans also helps agents, so far this has been my expereince and observations.  AI agents makes thisng  artifacts reu-usable, and reproducible these artifacts to automate a business workflow. Next, as I adopted AI first coding I also created lots of planning, prompt, and specifications docuemnts, which had lots of semantic knoweledge buried in there and scattered. Quite often I had to do naviagte these files to hunt for specific infromation like why i decided to have default config parameter this not this. That lead to motivation to find more sustainable solution and solution was simple and lying to right infron of me Wiki [@karpathy_llm_wiki_2026, @ond]. I did not need more files; I needed stronger relationships between ideas, code, and decisions.

This project started with motivation I wanted a way to preserve context so an agent can reason with it, not just search it. Sharing this template to broader community if the current template finds utility in there workflow. 

## Method

`wiki_code_space` treats code as a medium for organizing thought. It combines a lightweight wiki, semantic links, and repeatable update flows so rationale stays connected to implementation. 

The wiki folder is organized as an Obsidian vault markdown syntax so can be opened in Obsidian as an vault for easier human navigationa and reading. The wiki is a living document: it is updated as code changes, and it is versioned alongside the code. The wiki is also a source of truth for agents: it can be queried, reasoned over, and used to generate new code. The current template is designed for quantitative workflows, but the principles are broadly applicable. Also, the prompt design is geared towards graphifyy packages [@graphify_labs_graphify_2026] semantic relations capture, so that when graphify runs a graph build out it integrates these infromation in graph nodes and edges along with better community grouping.

The goal is agent-first development: use tools that keep concepts, decisions, and code in one navigable structure. This is not a bulletproof recipe. It is a practical template you can adapt to your own quantitative analysis stack.

## Conclusion

The core idea is simple: when semantic relationships are explicit, both humans and agents work better. This template is meant to inspire a shift in how we build analytical systems: not only writing code that runs, but writing code that remembers why it exists.
